unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 11-LEVEL: B1.3 THEME 5: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, CITY & SOCIAL LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore the theme "life in the neighbourhood, city and social life" with a focus on types of cities (such as slow cities and sustainable cities) and social life in rural and urban areas. Students will prepare a written and visual project comparing the lifestyles, social interactions, and environmental approaches in different city types and rural areas. They will describe the key features of slow cities and sustainable cities, highlighting their benefits and challenges. Additionally, they will examine how social life varies between rural and urban settings, considering factors like community engagement, cultural events, and daily routines. The project should include examples from real-life cities or neighbourhoods and propose ways to improve social cohesion and sustainability in their own communities. Students will present their findings through a creative format, such as a digital presentation or a poster. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city & social life with its components such as types of cities (slow cities, sustainable cities…); social life in the rural areas and cities'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 11 may know what types of cities (slow cities, sustainable cities…); social life in the rural areas and cities mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 11, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the neighbourhood, city & social life'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''air pollution, traffic jam, public transport, cultural, city and so on'' and also some structures such as ''What have you done at home since yesterday evening? I have cleaned our house.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city & social life with its components such as types of cities (slow cities, sustainable cities…) social life in the rural areas and cities'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about types of cities, social life in the rural areas and cities in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Match, Identify, and Build up The teacher introduces the activity. Students start by matching a picture to its descriptive sentence. For example, you might see a picture of a green park and match it with the description ''a relaxing and refreshing area with trees and fresh air''. Once they’ve made the match, identify the related word, like ''green city''. Then, write their own sentence using the word, such as, ''This green city has many parks for people to enjoy''. The teacher provides feedback on accuracy, use of target vocabulary, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe types of cities, social life in the rural areas and cities in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Picture Match and Speak The teacher introduces the activity. S/he shows a series of pictures related to types of cities, social life in the rural areas and cities, and the vocabulary words and explains the task. ''Match each vocabulary word with the correct picture and then create a sentence about the picture''. For example, if you see a park with many trees, you could say, ''The green city has many parks, and people can relax there''. Then, the teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
